mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement M139 PHEV engine for a C63 Hybrid typically costs between £4,500 and £18,000 depending on condition and whether the hybrid system is included. Used units start from £4,500-£8,000, reconditioned from £8,000-£13,000, and fully rebuilt from £10,000-£18,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 for AMG-specialist work. Hybrid engine replacements are among the most costly due to the complexity of the system.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C63 Hybrid uses the M139 engine, which has a timing chain, not a belt. The chain is designed to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance. However, the extreme power density of the M139 - producing 469 hp from 2.0 litres - places significant stress on all internal components. Regular oil changes using the correct AMG-approved oil spec are essential to maximise chain life.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs of engine problems in the C63 Hybrid include: intermittent power loss or a check engine light (hybrid system software issues), reduced electric range (battery degradation), oil spots under the car or burning oil smell (gasket leaks), overheating after spirited driving (cooling system strain), and starting issues (12V or high-voltage battery failure). If you experience any of these, have the car inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and mileage. A W206 C63 Hybrid is typically worth £50,000-£85,000 - a rebuilt M139 PHEV engine (£10,000-£18,000) is usually well within the car's value and can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. For lower-value examples or those with multiple issues, a specialist repair may be more economical than a full replacement.

mainEntity.name: Why did Mercedes-AMG replace the V8 with a four-cylinder hybrid in the C63?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C63 Hybrid replaced the twin-turbo V8 with a 2.0-litre four-cylinder M139 engine combined with an electric motor to meet stricter emissions regulations while maintaining high performance. The resulting 671 hp and 1,020 Nm of torque make it the most powerful C-Class ever. However, the decision has been controversial, with many enthusiasts criticising the loss of V8 character. Mercedes-AMG has admitted the four-cylinder PHEV failed to connect with customers and plans to phase it out.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the C63 Hybrid is most commonly caused by hybrid system software issues, which have led to recalls. Other causes include high-voltage battery degradation, electric motor control module failure, and cooling system issues affecting the electric exhaust gas turbocharger. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR/XENTRY or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class C63 Hybrid - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C63 Hybrid - officially the Mercedes-AMG C63 S E Performance - arrived in 2022 as the most powerful C-Class ever produced, and one of the most controversial AMG models in history. It replaced the legendary twin-turbo V8 with a hand-built 2.0-litre four-cylinder M139 engine paired with a rear-axle electric motor, producing a combined 671 hp and 1,020 Nm of torque. The powertrain incorporates technology derived from Mercedes-AMG's Formula 1 programme, including an electric exhaust gas turbocharger that reduces lag. Despite its staggering performance figures, the C63 Hybrid has faced criticism from enthusiasts who miss the V8's character.

milestones.description: M139 2.0L turbo PHEV, 671 hp (500 kW) combined - C63 S E Performance launch; 1,020 Nm torque; 0-62 mph in 3.4 seconds; 6.1 kWh battery; electric-only range of approximately 8 miles
UK deliveries commence; 9-speed AMG SPEEDSHIFT MCT 9G transmission; AMG Performance 4MATIC+ with Drift Mode
Facelift with revised hybrid software calibration; electric motor output remains 150 kW (201 hp)
Reports emerge that Mercedes-AMG will phase out the M139 PHEV system due to poor customer reception
Production ends; replaced by six-cylinder hybrid powertrain in next-generation C63

problems.group: M139 PHEV Hybrid System Software & Calibration Issues
problems.h4: M139 PHEV Hybrid System Software & Calibration Issues - Powertrain Malfunctions
problems.rootCause: The C63 Hybrid's complex hybrid system relies on sophisticated software to manage the interplay between the combustion engine and electric motor. Both V8 and turbo-four versions of the AMG E Performance PHEV drive system have been recalled, with the issue being software for the electric motor. Symptoms include intermittent power loss, check engine lights, and reduced performance. The electric motor's 150 kW output can be affected by calibration faults.

The engine is hand-built under AMG's "One Man, One Engine" philosophy, but the extreme power density places significant stress on seals.
